thread:
marta: Heads-up: after the v1.13 rollout we're seeing a reproducible perf regression tied to continuous batching interacting with the KV cache. Long-context jobs (8k+ tokens) slowly ramp GPU memory (+~1.8GB over ~10m) and intermittently hit p99 latency spikes. Loadtest: stable qps, but throughput drops ~30% at p99. stack image: runtime v1.12.3 -> v1.13.0.

cj: thanks. any quick profiles / counters? sounds like either fragmentation + pager evictions, or merge logic holding onto head fragments.

marta: attaching repro command and a flamegraph link from the canary run. quick repro:
```bash
# run loadgen with long ctx
./loadgen --model redwood-llama-13b --seq 8192 --concurrency 16 --continuous-batching
```
flamegraph: https://internal.profiler/fg/2769512345 (uploaded)

eli: looked at the flame - a bunch of time in `kv_pager::merge_and_rewrite` and `cont_batch::wait_for_merge`. counters snapshot: `kv_pager_evictions=412`, `kv_fragmentation_ratio=1.7`, `cont_batch_merge_waits=98` during the 10m window. pager churn is high and merge holds appear to serialize progress, creating hol-like head blocking where newer requests stall behind a merge that copies fragments.

profiler-bot: Generated differential flamegraph between v1.12.3 and v1.13.0: https://internal.profiler/diff/2769512345 (major diff in KV merge path) :mag:

cj: if merge holds locks while copying, continuous-batching merge heuristic might be coalescing too aggressively. two quick experiments: 1) lower merge window so merges don't span large frag sets, 2) force merge to be async-copy + swap to reduce hold time. try env `CONT_BATCH_MERGE_MS=5` or `KV_MERGE_ASYNC=1` and run same loadtest.

marta: ran quick smoke: `CONT_BATCH_MERGE_MS=5` reduced p99 by ~40% and lowered `cont_batch_merge_waits` to 12. memory still creeping but at slower rate (~+600MB over 10m).

eli: that aligns with an HOL stall hypothesis. when merge spans many fragments we keep refs to KV pages, preventing reclaim and causing pager thrash. also suspect kernel selection path change in v1.13 that increased per-token transient allocations during merge. I'll collect allocator traces.

infra-bot: canary v1.13.1 created for further testing (canary-id: canary-2026-03-18-17).

cj: next steps: eli to capture allocator + pagefault trace, marta to run knob matrix (merge_ms, async merge toggles) across canary, i'll open an issue to track (ENG-rr/4321) and add a small test to loadgen that stresses long-context merge scenarios. if anyone finds an easy short-term mitigator we can patch canary quickly. :thumbsup:

marta: noted. I'll post updated flamegraphs + counter dumps in the issue. thanks!
